title_en: Beijing Changfu Investment Fund v. Wuhan Zhongsenhua Century Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. et al. — dispute over an entrusted loan contract
ruling_gist_en: An entrustment loan contract is entered into by and among the principal, the agent bank, and the borrower, under which the principal provides funds, the agent bank lends on behalf of the principal, assists in supervising the use of the loan, and recovers the loan in accordance with the borrower, purpose, amount, currency, term, and interest rate determined by the principal. The agent bank collects a handling fee for acting as an agent for the entrustment loan and does not assume credit risk. The substance of such arrangement is a private lending between the principal and the borrower. The validity of the entrustment loan contract, and the rights and obligations between the principal and the borrower concerning interest, overdue interest, liquidated damages, etc., shall all be governed by the laws, regulations, and judicial interpretations related to private lending.

full_text_en:
Beijing Changfu Investment Fund v. Wuhan Zhongsenhua Century Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. et al. — dispute over entrusted loan contract

【Ruling Summary】

Where a principal, a trustee bank, and a borrower enter into an entrusted loan contract, with the principal providing the funds and the trustee bank, based on the borrower, purpose, amount, currency, term, interest rate, and other matters determined by the principal, disbursing the loan, assisting in monitoring its use, and recovering it, and the trustee bank charging a handling fee for the entrusted loan and assuming no credit risk, the substance of the arrangement is a private lending between the principal and the borrower. The validity of the entrusted loan contract, and the rights and obligations between the principal and the borrower regarding interest, overdue interest, liquidated damages, and other matters, shall all be governed by the laws, regulations, and judicial interpretations relating to private lending.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2016) Supreme People's Court Final Civil Judgment No. 124

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Beijing Changfu Investment Fund (Limited Partnership). Domicile: Room 501-09, Building 1, No. 18 Lize Road, Fengtai District, Beijing.

Representative: Tong Tiecheng, representative appointed by the executive partner.

Agent ad litem: Wan Qinzhong, lawyer, Hubei Haoze Law Firm.

Legal Representative: Zheng Juyun, executive director of the company.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Liyan, lawyer, Beijing Shangge Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Liu Jinlan, trainee lawyer, Beijing Shangge Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Zhongsenhua Investment Group Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 100 Chezhan Road, Jiangan District, Wuhan, Hubei Province.

Legal Representative: Zheng Juyun, chairman of the board of the company.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Liyan, lawyer, Beijing Shangge Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Liu Jinlan, trainee lawyer, Beijing Shangge Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Zheng Juyun, male, Han ethnicity, domiciled in Yueqing City, Zhejiang Province.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Chen Shaoxia, female, Han ethnicity, domiciled in Yueqing City, Zhejiang Province.

Respondent (Third Party at First Instance): Hubei Xudong (Group) Co., Ltd. Domicile: Rooms B603-610, Building 9, Fashion Oropa, No. 508 Youyi Avenue, Hongshan District, Wuhan, Hubei Province.

Representative: Zeng Xiaoyang, branch manager.

Agent ad litem: Liang Shulan, staff member of the branch.

Agent ad litem: Tian Hui, staff member of the branch.

Third Party at First Instance: Beilong Construction Group Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 198-1 Tanxi Road, Xiangcheng District, Xiangyang, Hubei Province.
