Legal Representative: Liu Weihong, general manager of the company.

Third Party at First Instance: Fujian Zhongsen Construction Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 20 Wusi Road, Yong'an City, Fujian Province.

Legal Representative: Chen Donghai, chairman of the board of the company.

Agent ad litem: Fan Dingbao, lawyer, Fujian Yonghang Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Liu Chunlong, lawyer, Fujian Yonghang Law Firm.

The Appellants, Beijing Changfu Investment Fund (Limited Partnership) (hereinafter referred to as Changfu Fund) and Wuhan Zhongsenhua Century Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company), appealed to this Court against the civil judgment (2014) E Er Min Chu Zi No. 00035 of the Hubei High People's Court in the case of contract dispute with the Respondents, Zhongsenhua Investment Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhongsenhua Investment Company), Zheng Juyun, Chen Shaoxia, and Hubei Xudong (Group) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xudong Group Company), as well as the Third Parties at First Instance, Industrial Bank Co., Ltd., Wuhan Branch (hereinafter referred to as Industrial Bank Wuhan Branch), Beilong Construction Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Beilong Company), Hubei Xianghe Construction Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xianghe Company), and Fujian Zhongsen Construction Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhongsen Company). This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, with Judge Huang Nian serving as the presiding judge, and Judge Li Jingping and Acting Judge Li Zhigang participating in the trial, and Court Clerk Wuning Yuqi serving as the record keeper. The trial of this case has now been concluded.

The facts found at first instance are as follows:

On September 27, 2013, Changfu Fund, Industrial Bank Wuhan Branch, Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company, Zhongsenhua Investment Company, Zheng Juyun, and Chen Shaoxia entered into an "Investment Cooperation Agreement," stipulating that Changfu Fund would entrust Industrial Bank Wuhan Branch to disburse a loan of RMB 630 million to Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company by way of entrusted loan for the completion of the urban village comprehensive renovation project in Xudong Village, with the loan to be disbursed in two tranches. The agreement also provided for matters such as loan guarantee, conditions for disbursement, supervision, liability for breach, and dispute resolution. On the same day, Changfu Fund, Industrial Bank Wuhan Branch, and Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company entered into an "Entrusted Loan Contract," stipulating that Changfu Fund would entrust Industrial Bank Wuhan Branch to lend RMB 630 million to Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company, for the purpose of the Xudong Village urban village comprehensive renovation project, with the loan to be disbursed in two tranches. The disbursement timelines and conditions were as follows: The first tranche of RMB 400 million was to be disbursed subject to the conditions that "Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company enters into an agreement or contract with Hubei Zhujiang Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. for the purchase of all land use rights (approximately 20 mu) owned by Hubei Zhujiang Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. and obtains a general notarized attestation; Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company mortgages to Industrial Bank Wuhan Branch the land use right of parcel K1 located in Xudong Village, Hongshan District, Wuhan, with an area of 25,134.12 square meters (Certificate No. Wu Guo Yong (2012) No. X1), and the construction in progress of parcel K5 with an area of 10,313.48 square meters and the land use right of parcel K5 with an area of 5,424.82 square meters (Certificate No. Wu Guo Yong (2012) No. X2) (see the "Mortgage Property List" attached to the "Mortgage Contract" for details), and the mortgage registration procedures are completed; Zhongsenhua Investment Company provides pledge guarantee for the entire debt of Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company under this agreement by pledging its 49% equity to Industrial Bank Wuhan Branch, and the pledge registration procedures are completed." The second tranche of RMB 230 million was to be disbursed subject to the conditions that "Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company mortgages to Industrial Bank Wuhan Branch the land use right of parcel K2 located in Xudong Village, Hongshan District, Wuhan, with an area of 4,359.22 square meters (Certificate No. Wu Guo Yong (2012) No. X3), the land use right of parcel K3 with an area of 15,436.26 square meters (Certificate No. Wu Guo Yong (2012) No. X4), the construction in progress of parcel K4 with an area of 35,303.85 square meters and the land use right of parcel K4 with an area of 7,933 square meters (Certificate No. Wu Guo Yong (2013) No. X5), and the mortgage registration procedures are completed." The loan term under the contract was four years, commencing from the date of disbursement of the first tranche, and regardless of when the second tranche was disbursed, it would mature at the same time as the first tranche. The loan interest rate was 16% per annum for the first to third years, and 18% per annum for the fourth year, with interest settled quarterly, and the settlement date being the first working day after the 20th day of the last month of each calendar quarter. The contract also provided for default interest, stipulating that "if the borrower fails to repay the principal and interest within the time limit agreed in the contract, the principal shall charge default interest on the overdue amount from the date of default at a rate 50% above the agreed loan interest rate until full repayment of principal and interest." Article 4 of the "Entrusted Loan Contract" stipulated that acts constituting default by the borrower included: failure to perform the commitments made under Article 1 of the contract; expressly indicating or demonstrating by conduct a refusal to repay its due or undue debts; failure to perform or fully perform obligations under other contracts entered into with the principal; the principal declaring the borrower in default; or other circumstances where the borrower fails to perform or fully perform the contract. Article 4 also provided for the circumstances and conditions for taking remedial measures, including where the borrower or guarantor defaults; where the repayment capacity of the borrower or guarantor may undergo major adverse changes, or the mortgaged or pledged property may suffer material damage or diminution in value, etc. The remedial measures that could be taken included suspending the disbursement of the loan, accelerating the repayment of the disbursed loan, requiring the borrower to bear damages and other legal liabilities, and taking corresponding asset preservation measures and other legal measures. The contract also stipulated that if the borrower's default caused the principal to take legal proceedings or arbitration to realize its claims, the borrower shall bear the legal fees, litigation costs, travel expenses, enforcement fees, and other necessary costs incurred by the principal for realizing its claims.

Subsequently, Industrial Bank Wuhan Branch and Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company entered into five "Mortgage Contracts," stipulating that Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company would provide mortgage security to Industrial Bank Wuhan Branch over the land use right of parcel K1 located in Xudong Village, Hongshan District, Wuhan, with an area of 25,134.12 square meters (Certificate No. Wu Guo Yong (2012) No. X1), the land use right of parcel K2 with an area of 4,359.22 square meters (Certificate No. Wu Guo Yong (2012) No. X3), the land use right of parcel K3 with an area of 15,436.26 square meters (Certificate No. Wu Guo Yong (2012) No. X4), the construction in progress of parcel K4 with an area of 35,303.85 square meters and the land use right of parcel K4 with an area of 7,933 square meters (Certificate No. Wu Guo Yong (2013) No. X5), and the construction in progress of parcel K5 with an area of 10,325.82 square meters and the land use right of parcel K5 with an area of 5,424.82 square meters (Certificate No. Wu Guo Yong (2012) No. X2). The scope of the guarantee covered all claims under the master contract, including but not limited to principal, interest, liquidated damages, compensation, other amounts payable by the debtor to the borrower, and costs incurred by Industrial Bank Wuhan Branch in enforcing claims and security rights.

Thereafter, Industrial Bank Wuhan Branch also entered into an "Equity Pledge Contract" with Zhongsenhua Investment Company, stipulating that Zhongsenhua Investment Company would provide security for the principal debt of RMB 630 million and interest under the master contract by pledging its 49% equity in Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company. After the equity pledge contract was signed, the parties registered the pledge on November 26, 2013, at the Administration for Industry and Commerce of Hongshan District, Wuhan, Hubei Province.

On September 27, 2013, Industrial Bank Wuhan Branch entered into a "Joint and Several Guarantee Contract" with Zhongsenhua Investment Company, Zheng Juyun, and Chen Shaoxia, stipulating that Zhongsenhua Investment Company, Zheng Juyun, and Chen Shaoxia would provide guarantee for the principal loan of RMB 630 million and interest, liquidated damages, compensation, etc. of the debtor Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company, in the form of irrevocable joint and several liability guarantee, with a guarantee period of two years, commencing from the date of maturity of the debt under the master contract. If the master contract provided that the debtor was declared due early by the lender due to agreed events, the guarantee period commenced from the date of early maturity of the debt under the master contract.

After the above contracts were signed, the parties registered the mortgage on the land use right of parcel K1 with an area of 25,134.12 square meters (Certificate No. Wu Guo Yong (2012) No. X1) and the land use right of parcel K5 with an area of 5,424.82 square meters (Certificate No. Wu Guo Yong (2012) No. X2) at the Wuhan Municipal Bureau of Land Resources and Planning, Hubei Province, and registered the mortgage on the construction in progress of 10,325.82 square meters at the Housing Security and Administration Bureau of Hongshan District, Wuhan, Hubei Province. On December 12, 2013, Changfu Fund disbursed the first tranche of the entrusted loan of RMB 400 million to Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company through Industrial Bank Wuhan Branch. On March 21, 2014, Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company paid interest of RMB 16 million to Changfu Fund through Industrial Bank Wuhan Branch. Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company did not handle the mortgage registration for the land use rights and construction in progress of parcels K2, K3, and K4, and Industrial Bank Wuhan Branch did not disburse the second tranche of RMB 230 million.

Changfu Fund filed this lawsuit, alleging that Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company failed to handle the mortgage on the land use rights and construction in progress of parcels K2, K3, and K4 as agreed in the "Entrusted Loan Contract" and the "Mortgage Contracts," and most of the mortgaged construction in progress had been sold, constituting a default, and it should bear liability for breach and pay liquidated damages to Changfu Fund. Changfu Fund also alleged that Zhongsenhua Investment Company, Zheng Juyun, and Chen Shaoxia should bear the pledge guarantee liability and joint and several guarantee liability. Changfu Fund requested the court to: 1. Terminate the performance of the "Entrusted Loan Contract" signed between Changfu Fund, Industrial Bank Wuhan Branch, and Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company, and accelerate the repayment of the loan. 2. Order Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company to repay the loan principal of RMB 400 million and interest of RMB 16.18 million (interest calculated from March 22 to June 21, 2014, at the annual rate of 16%), and from June 22, 2014, interest calculated at the annual rate of 16% x (1 + 50%) until full repayment of principal and interest. 3. Order Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company to bear liability for breach and pay liquidated damages of RMB 126 million. 4. Affirm that Changfu Fund has priority in compensation over the land use right of 25,134.12 square meters located in Xudong Village, Hongshan District, Wuhan, covered by the security right certificate Wu Ta Xiang (2013) No. X6, and over the land use right of 5,424.82 square meters covered by the security right certificate Wu Ta Xiang (2013) No. X7, and over the 10,325.82 square meters of buildings covered by the Wuhan city forward housing mortgage certificate (Wu Fang Qi Hong Zi No. 2013015485) in Xudong Village, Hongshan District, Xudong Apartments. 5. Affirm that Changfu Fund has priority in compensation over the 49% equity in Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company pledged by Zhongsenhua Investment Company. 6. Order Zhongsenhua Investment Company, Zheng Juyun, and Chen Shaoxia to bear joint and several liability for repayment of the debts in items 2 and 3. 7. Order the disposal of all of Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company's rights and interests in the industrial project of Block C of the Xudong Village urban village comprehensive renovation project in Xudong Group Company to satisfy the debts in this case. 8. Confirm that the "Letter of Undertaking" (No. 2013 (Century) Zi No. 7-1) of August 2013 from Beilong Company is legally valid and that Beilong Company's right to be compensated for construction project building fees in the Xudong Village urban village comprehensive renovation project of Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company is junior to Changfu Fund's claims. 9. Confirm that the "Letter of Undertaking" (No. 2013 (Century) Zi No. 7-4) of August 26, 2013, from Xianghe Company is legally valid and that Xianghe Company's right to be compensated for construction project building fees in the Xudong Village urban village comprehensive renovation project of Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company is junior to Changfu Fund's claims. 10. Confirm that the "Letter of Undertaking" (No. 2013 (Century) Zi No. 7-5) of August 26, 2013, from Zhongsen Company is legally valid and that Zhongsen Company's right to be compensated for construction project building fees in the Xudong Village urban village comprehensive renovation project of Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company is junior to Changfu Fund's claims. 11. Order the defendants to bear all litigation costs in this case.

Additionally, the facts found are: Xudong Group Company issued a "Letter of Undertaking" to Changfu Fund, stating: "All claims held by this company against Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company are junior to the principal, interest, and other related rights and interests that your party enjoys under the RMB 630 million financing provided to Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company by way of entrusted loan." Xianghe Company issued a "Letter of Undertaking" to Changfu Fund, stating: "This company's right to be compensated for construction project building fees on the aforementioned K2, K3, C2, C3, and C4 project works is junior to the principal, interest, and other related rights and interests that your party enjoys under the RMB 630 million financing provided to Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company by way of entrusted loan." The Wuhan Zhongxing Notary Office of Hubei Province issued "Notarial Certificates" for both of the above "Letters of Undertaking."

On November 26, 2014, the Wuhan Zhongxing Notary Office of Hubei Province issued a "Decision on Revoking the Notarial Certificate (2013) E Zhong Xing Nei Zheng Zi No. 19246" (2014) E Zhong Xing Jue Zi No. 6, stating: The seal of Beilong Company and the signature of its legal representative Chen Shutian on the "Letter of Undertaking" numbered 2013 (Century) Zi No. 7-1 were both forged. Our office decides to revoke the Notarial Certificate (2013) E Zhong Xing Nei Zheng Zi No. 19246. This notarial certificate is null and void ab initio.

During the trial of the court of first instance, the Urban-rural Coordinated Development Work Office of Jiangan District, Wuhan, Hubei Province raised an objection, stating: The buildings on parcel K4 with a construction area of 35,303.85 square meters and the forward housing (Xudong Apartments) of 10,325.82 square meters that had been registered as mortgages on parcel K5, which were subject to the preservation measures applied for by Changfu Fund, had already been sold to this office.

The court of first instance held that: the "Investment Cooperation Agreement," "Entrusted Loan Contract," "Mortgage Contract," "Equity Pledge Contract," and "Joint and Several Guarantee Contract" involved in this case represent the true intentions of the parties, and their contents do not violate the prohibitive provisions of laws and regulations. They should be recognized as legal and valid. All parties should strictly perform their respective obligations in accordance with the contracts. Industrial Bank Wuhan Branch, entrusted by Changfu Fund, issued the entrusted loan to Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company. The three parties established an entrusted loan contractual relationship through the contracts entered into between them. Article 402 of the Contract Law of the PRC provides: "If the agent enters into a contract with a third party in his own name within the scope of authorization, and if the third party, at the time of entering into the contract, is aware of the agency relationship between the agent and the principal, the contract shall directly bind the principal and the third party, unless there is conclusive evidence that the contract binds only the agent and the third party." Because Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company was fully aware of the fact that the entrusted loan was issued by Industrial Bank Wuhan Branch on behalf of Changfu Fund, the "Entrusted Loan Contract" directly binds Changfu Fund and Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company. Changfu Fund may assert its rights directly against Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company in its own name. In this case, listing Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company as the defendant and Industrial Bank Wuhan Branch as the third party complies with legal provisions. The nominal rights holders under the "Mortgage Contract," "Equity Pledge Contract," "Joint and Several Guarantee Contract," and the mortgage and pledge registrations in this case are Industrial Bank Wuhan Branch. However, because Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company and the guarantors were aware that the actual rights holder of the loan issued by Industrial Bank Wuhan Branch on behalf of Changfu Fund and the guarantees was Changfu Fund, and because Industrial Bank Wuhan Branch does not object to Changfu Fund directly asserting the security rights, the guarantee contracts in this case should directly bind Changfu Fund, Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company, and the guarantors. Changfu Fund has a priority right to be reimbursed from the proceeds from the disposal of the collateral provided by Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company and other guarantors for its creditor's rights.

Changfu Fund requested the termination of the "Entrusted Loan Contract" and the early recovery of the loan, and expressly stated that this claim was based on Article 93 of the Contract Law of the PRC, which essentially means requesting the rescission of the contract. The court of first instance held that Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company failed to complete the mortgage registration for Plots K2, K3, K4 and the project under construction as agreed, which constitutes a "failure to perform or complete performance of obligations under other contracts entered into between the borrower and the principal." Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company failed to pay interest quarterly as stipulated in the contract; after paying interest for the first quarter of 2014, it ceased paying interest from March 22, 2014, which constitutes an "express statement or conduct indicating unwillingness to repay its matured or unmatured debts." When the court of first instance implemented the preservation of assets in this case, Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company was already involved in multiple lawsuits, and the collateral provided to Changfu Fund had been seized by other creditors. Therefore, Changfu Fund's request to terminate the contract and recover the loan early complies with the agreement in the "Investment Agreement" and "Entrusted Loan Contract" that "if the borrower or guarantor defaults, the borrower's or guarantor's repayment ability may undergo material adverse changes, the collateral or pledged property may suffer material damage or decrease in value, etc., the loan may be suspended, and the loan already disbursed may be recovered early." The court of first instance supported this claim of Changfu Fund in accordance with the law.

Article 97 of the Contract Law of the PRC provides: "After the rescission of a contract, for the part not yet performed, performance shall be terminated; for the part already performed, depending on the circumstances and nature of the contract, the parties may request restoration to the original state, take other remedial measures, and have the right to claim compensation for losses." Accordingly, after the rescission of the "Entrusted Loan Contract" in this case, the unperformed part of the loan amounting to RMB 230 million shall cease to be performed. Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company shall return the principal of the entrusted loan of RMB 400 million already disbursed to Changfu Fund and compensate Changfu Fund for its losses. The losses are the legally expected income Changfu Fund could have obtained from this transaction, calculated based on the principal of RMB 400 million already disbursed and the agreed annual interest rate of 16% from the date of disbursement until the date on which Changfu Fund filed the lawsuit requesting termination of the contract. Interest thereafter shall be calculated according to the agreed overdue interest rate. Changfu Fund requested payment of liquidated damages of RMB 126 million, i.e., 20% of the principal of the entrusted loan as stipulated in the mortgage contract. Because the above interest is already sufficient to compensate Changfu Fund for the losses incurred due to the rescission of the contract, the court of first instance did not support this claim.

The seal of Beilong Company and the signature of its legal representative, Chen Shutian, on Beilong Company's "Letter of Commitment" were determined by the Hubei Provincial Wuhan Zhongxing Notary Office to be forgeries. Upon examination, the seal impression of Zhongsen Company on its "Letter of Commitment" was not formed by the seal actually used by Zhongsen Company, and the signature of Chen Tonghai, the legal representative of Zhongsen Company, on the "Letter of Commitment" was not written by Chen Tonghai. Therefore, the contents of the two "Letters of Commitment" submitted by Changfu Fund cannot be deemed to represent the true intentions of Beilong Company and Zhongsen Company, and they are not binding on Beilong Company and Zhongsen Company. Xudong Group and Xianghe Company issued written commitments to Changfu Fund, promising that their claims for construction project costs would be subordinate to Changfu Fund's claims. These commitments reflect the true intentions of Xudong Group and Xianghe Company, and there is no circumstance rendering the legal acts invalid as provided by law. They should be recognized as valid. Xianghe Company argued that its commitment to waive the priority right of compensation was not its true intention, but did not submit evidence to prove this, nor did it request an appraisal. Xianghe Company argued that the priority right of compensation for construction project costs is a statutory security right, and a commitment to subordinate the priority right of compensation to other creditors' claims harms the legitimate rights and interests of others and is therefore invalid. The court of first instance held that the purpose of the statutory priority right of compensation for construction project costs is to protect the realization of legitimate rights and interests such as workers' wages, but it is still a civil right that the right holder can freely dispose of. Xianghe Company's claim that its voluntary commitment is invalid violates the principle of good faith, and the court of first instance did not support it. As for whether Xudong Group and Xianghe Company have any claims for construction project costs against Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company, the amounts and scope of such claims, and whether Changfu Fund has the right to dispose of Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company's interests in the C-block industrial project under Xudong Group's Xudong Village renovation project to satisfy the debts in this case, these are not within the scope of trial in this case and should be resolved in a separate case or during the enforcement stage.

In summary, some of Changfu Fund's claims are in accordance with the law and are supported. Pursuant to Article 106, paragraph 1, and Article 108 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC; Articles 8, 60, paragraph 1, 93, and 97 of the Contract Law of the PRC; Articles 18, 33, 46, and 75 of the Security Law of the PRC; and Article 142 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the court of first instance hereby rules as follows:
1. The "Entrusted Loan Contract" signed on September 27, 2013, among Changfu Fund, Industrial Bank Wuhan Branch, and Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company is rescinded.
2. Within fifteen days of the effective date of this judgment, Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company shall repay the principal of the entrusted loan of RMB 400 million to Changfu Fund and compensate for interest losses (with RMB 400 million as the base, interest shall be calculated at an annual rate of 16% from March 22, 2014, to September 9, 2014, and at an annual rate of 24% from September 10, 2014, until the date of actual payment as determined by this judgment).
3. Changfu Fund has the right to be reimbursed in priority from the proceeds of the discount, auction, or sale of the land use rights of 25,134.12 square meters located in Xudong Village, Hongshan District, Wuhan City, under the Other Right Certificate Wu Ta Other (2013) No. X6; the land use rights of 5,424.82 square meters located in Xudong Village, Hongshan District, Wuhan City, under the Other Right Certificate Wu Ta Other (2013) No. X7; and the houses of 10,325.82 square meters located at Xudong Apartment, Xudong Village, Hongshan District, Wuhan City, under the Wuhan City Forward Housing Mortgage Certificate (Wu Fang Qi Hong Zi No. 2013015485), for the claims determined in Item 2 of this judgment.
4. Changfu Fund has the right to be reimbursed in priority from the proceeds of the discount, auction, or sale of the 49% equity interest held by Zhongsenhua Investment Company in Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company, for the claims determined in Item 2 of this judgment.
5. Zhongsenhua Investment Company, Zheng Juyun, and Chen Shaoxia shall assume joint and several liability for the debts of Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company determined in Item 2 of this judgment. After assuming the guarantee liability, Zhongsenhua Investment Company, Zheng Juyun, and Chen Shaoxia have the right to seek recourse from Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company.
6. Confirm that the "Letter of Commitment" (No. 2013 (Century) Zi No. 7-4) issued by Xianghe Company to Changfu Fund is valid.
7. Dismiss all other claims of Changfu Fund.

Court acceptance fee: RMB 2,752,700; preservation fee: RMB 5,000, totaling RMB 2,757,700. Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company shall bear RMB 2,206,160; Changfu Fund shall bear RMB 546,540. Appraisal fee: RMB 110,000, to be borne by Changfu Fund.

Changfu Fund, dissatisfied with the judgment of the court of first instance, appealed to this Court, requesting: 1. Uphold Items 1, 2, and 6 of the original judgment, modify Item 7 of the original judgment, and additionally rule that Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company shall pay liquidated damages of RMB 126 million; 2. Modify the reference to "the claims determined in Item 2 of this judgment" in Items 3, 4, and 5 of the original judgment to include both the claims in Item 2 of the original judgment and the liquidated damages of RMB 126 million; 3. Rule that the "Letter of Commitment" issued by Xudong Group is legal and valid, and that Changfu Fund has the right to dispose of all of Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company's interests in the C-block industrial project under Xudong Group's Xudong Village urban village comprehensive renovation project to satisfy the debts of this case; 4. Rule that Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company shall bear the appraisal fee of RMB 110,000; 5. Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company shall bear all litigation costs for the first instance and the second instance. The main reasons are: 1. Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company violated the provisions of the "Investment Cooperation Agreement," "Entrusted Loan Contract," and "Mortgage Contract" by failing to complete the mortgage registration for the mortgaged property, resulting in its seizure by others. Moreover, it sold the property for which mortgage registration had already been completed without depositing the proceeds of more than RMB 215.81 million into the supervisory account, constituting a serious breach of contract. It should bear liability for breach of contract and pay liquidated damages of RMB 126 million as stipulated in the contract. The first-instance judgment found Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company to be in breach, but did not support Changfu Fund's claim for liquidated damages on the grounds that the interest already awarded was sufficient to compensate Changfu Fund for the losses incurred due to the rescission of the contract. This fails to reflect the punishment for the breach and should be corrected. 2. The "Joint Development Contract for the Comprehensive Renovation of the 'Urban Village' in Xudong Village, Hongshan District, Wuhan City" between Xudong Group stipulated that Plot C would be invested and developed by Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company, and all investment rights and interests belonged to Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company. In a "Letter of Commitment" dated November 29, 2013, Xudong Group stated that except for 15,000 square meters of shops in Plot C, all other interests belonged to Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company. It agreed to waive its right to rescind the contract until Changfu Fund's claims were satisfied, and all of Xudong Group's claims against Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company would be subordinate to Changfu Fund's claims. Therefore, Changfu Fund has the right to dispose of all of Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company's interests in the C-block industrial project under Xudong Group's Xudong Village urban village comprehensive renovation project to satisfy the debts of this case. 3. The falsification of the official seal and signature on Zhongsen Company's "Letter of Commitment" was the act of Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company, and the appraisal fee should be borne by Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company.

Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company, Zhongsenhua Investment Company, Zheng Juyun, and Chen Shaoxia argued in their defense: 1. The loan amount stipulated in the "Entrusted Loan Contract" was RMB 630 million, but Changfu Fund only disbursed RMB 400 million. Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company had already mortgaged the land use rights of Plots K1 and K5 in Xudong Village to Changfu Fund for the RMB 400 million loan. Changfu Fund's failure to disburse the remaining RMB 230 million loan constituted a breach of contract. The loss for Changfu Fund regarding the RMB 400 million loan was purely interest loss, and the agreed annual interest rate of 16% on the loan was sufficient to compensate for it. 2. The "Joint Development Contract for the Comprehensive Renovation of the 'Urban Village' in Xudong Village" only defined the scope of rights between Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company and Xudong Group. The C-block industrial project was not registered under Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company's name. Whether Changfu Fund has the right to dispose of Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company's interests in the C-block industrial project is irrelevant to this case and exceeds the scope of this trial. 3. The "Letter of Commitment" from Zhongsen Company was evidence submitted by Changfu Fund. According to the principle of "whoever asserts, bears the burden," Changfu Fund should bear the appraisal fee. Moreover, Zhongsen Company had multiple seals; the fact that the seal on the "Letter of Commitment" did not match the sample seal used for appraisal does not necessarily prove it was forged. Additionally, although a "Letter of Commitment" was provided to Changfu Fund, it cannot be determined that the one appraised was the same one submitted by Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company. In summary, they requested the dismissal of Changfu Fund's appeal.

Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company, dissatisfied with the judgment of the court of first instance, appealed to this Court, requesting: 1. Modify Item 2 of the original judgment from "from September 10, 2014, until the date of actual payment as determined by this judgment at an annual rate of 24%" to "from September 10, 2014, until the date of actual payment as determined by this judgment at an annual rate of 16%"; 2. The litigation costs for the first instance and the second instance shall be borne by Changfu Fund. The main reasons: Changfu Fund breached the contract by failing to disburse the second tranche of RMB 230 million to Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company, causing financial difficulties for the project and significant losses to Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company. Changfu Fund should also bear responsibility for the rescission of the "Entrusted Loan Contract." The first-instance judgment's increase of the overdue annual interest rate to 24% failed to fairly allocate responsibility and imposed a heavier burden on Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company. The loan term agreed in the contract was four years, and the loan had not yet matured at the time Changfu Fund filed the lawsuit. Even if the contract were rescinded and the loan repaid, the loan should only be considered overdue after the expiration of the payment period determined by the judgment. The period from September 10, 2014, to the date of payment determined by the judgment is not an overdue period, so a penalty interest rate increased by 50% should not apply. During the second-instance court hearing, Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company submitted a supplementary appeal, requesting: Ruling to vacate the original judgment and dismiss the lawsuit. The main reason is: Clause 1.4 of the "Entrusted Loan Contract" stipulates, "If the borrower fails to repay the principal and interest on time, the agent shall, upon the principal's written request, file a lawsuit in the agent's name against the borrower, guarantor, and related parties." This clause is consistent with the Supreme People's Court's "Reply on How to Determine the Subject of Litigation in Entrusted Loan Agreement Disputes." In this case, Changfu Fund, as the principal, directly filed a lawsuit against Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company, which does not comply with the contractual agreement. The court of first instance should not have accepted the case.

Changfu Fund argued in its defense: 1. Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company's appeal argument that Changfu Fund is not a proper plaintiff in this case is untenable. (1) The final appeal deadline was December 25, 2015. Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company's appeal within the appeal period was directed at the issue of whether the annual interest rate was 16% or 24%, and it paid the appeal fee accordingly for that dispute; it did not pay the appeal fee for all claims. Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company's submission of this appeal claim during the second-instance court hearing on March 21, 2016, does not comply with Article 323 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC and should not be accepted. (2) From the contract terms, Changfu Fund is a fully qualified plaintiff. Article 5, Item 1 of the "Investment Cooperation Agreement" and Article 4.4 of the "Entrusted Loan Contract" explicitly stipulate that Changfu Fund has the right to file a lawsuit to assert its rights. Clause 1.4 of the "Entrusted Loan Contract" is an optional provision; Changfu Fund may file a lawsuit on its own or may request the agent to do so. It only binds the principal and the agent. 3. The Supreme People's Court's "Reply on How to Determine the Subject of Litigation in Entrusted Loan Agreement Disputes" does not provide that the principal cannot file a lawsuit as a plaintiff; it only addresses the status and liability of the agent bank as a defendant. Pursuant to Article 402 of the Contract Law of the PRC, the "Entrusted Loan Contract" directly binds Changfu Fund and Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company. 4. During the trial at the court of first instance, the agent bank explicitly agreed to Changfu Fund's assertion of rights. During the second-instance court hearing, Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company confirmed that it had no objection to the facts found and determined in the original judgment. 2. Changfu Fund disbursed the RMB 400 million loan in accordance with Article 2.1.3.1(1) of the "Entrusted Loan Contract," but Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company has still not completed the mortgage registration as stipulated, failing to meet the conditions for disbursing the second tranche of RMB 230 million as set out in Article 2.1.3.1(1). Changfu Fund is not in breach. On the contrary, Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company's breach caused the rescission of the "Investment Cooperation Agreement" and "Entrusted Loan Contract," and the responsibility lies entirely with Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company. 3. Article 2.1.7 of the "Entrusted Loan Contract" stipulates the conditions for penalty interest. Since March 22, 2014, Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company has failed to repay interest as stipulated, constituting a breach. It also failed to use the loan for the agreed purpose. Therefore, penalty interest at a rate increased by 50% should apply from the date Changfu Fund requested the rescission of the contract. In summary, Changfu Fund requested the dismissal of Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company's appeal.

Xudong Group argued in its defense: 1. Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company should not bear liquidated damages of RMB 126 million. Changfu Fund signed a fund supervisory agreement with the contracting parties. The loss was due to Changfu Fund's own failure to supervise. Changfu Fund's breach caused losses to Xudong Group. 2. The C-block industrial project in the Xudong Village urban village comprehensive renovation project is registered under Xudong Group's name. Only when three conditions for joint development are met can Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company obtain the property rights. The "Letter of Commitment" merely confirmed the possible rights of Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company in the plot. These rights are not facts to be determined in this case and should be resolved in a separate case or during the enforcement stage. Xudong Group requested the maintenance of the part of the original judgment concerning its interests.

Industrial Bank argued in its defense: 1. It agreed with Changfu Fund's defense regarding the plaintiff's qualifications. 2. Industrial Bank did not breach the contract. Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company's failure to fully perform the contract by completing mortgage registration for the relevant land, paying interest, and returning funds constitutes a breach and it should bear the losses.

Beilong Company argued in its defense: 1. Beilong Company never issued any commitment to subordinate its priority right of compensation for construction project costs to Changfu Fund or any third party. 2. The first-instance judgment determined that the "Letter of Commitment" from Beilong Company presented by Changfu Fund was forged, yet still ruled that Changfu Fund had a priority right over the proceeds from the auction of the Xudong Apartment project constructed by Beilong Company. This is contradictory and conflicts with the civil judgment of the Hubei High People's Court (2013) E Min Yi Chu Zi No. 00011. 3. Beilong Company was unnecessarily brought into the litigation as a third party, incurring substantial transportation, travel, and legal expenses. Changfu Fund should compensate Beilong Company RMB 100,000. In summary, Beilong Company requested the dismissal of Changfu Fund's claim for priority on the proceeds from the auction of the Xudong Apartment constructed by Beilong Company.

Xianghe Company did not appear in court and did not submit a defense.

Zhongsen Company responded in its defense: Zhongsen Company has no affiliation with Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company, and agrees with Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company's defense argument that the appraisal fees should be borne by Changfu Fund. It requests that Changfu Fund's appeal on this issue be dismissed.

The facts found by the court of first instance are affirmed by this court.

This court further finds that: In the five Mortgage Contracts involved in the case, Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company and Industrial Bank Wuhan Branch agreed as follows: If Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company conceals the true ownership status of the mortgaged property from Industrial Bank Wuhan Branch, for example, if Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company has no ownership or right of disposal over the mortgaged property; if the mortgaged property is mortgaged without the consent of other co-owners; if there is a dispute over the ownership of the mortgaged property; if the mortgaged property is sealed up or distrained; if Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company fails to cooperate with the mortgage registration procedures or fails to provide other equivalent security acceptable to Industrial Bank Wuhan Branch after the mortgaged property is accidentally damaged; if the mortgage right cannot be effectively established or cannot be asserted against a bona fide third party; if the mortgage ratio is insufficient and not replenished as agreed; or if the newly added part of the project under construction is not properly mortgaged, Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company shall pay liquidated damages to Party A equal to 20% of the principal of the debt under the master contract. If the liquidated damages are insufficient to compensate for the losses incurred by Industrial Bank Wuhan Branch, Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company shall be liable for compensation for the portion not covered by the liquidated damages.

In the Letter of Undertaking (2013) Century No. 12 issued to Changfu Fund, Xudong Group Company undertook the following: First, Zhongsenhua Investment Company and this company signed the Wuhan Hongshan District Xudong Village "Urban Village" Comprehensive Renovation Joint Development Contract in 2010. This company confirms that in the Xudong Village urban village comprehensive renovation project (including the K plot development project, the H plot resettlement project, and the C plot industrial project), Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company is entitled to all rights and interests in the land use rights, projects under construction, building ownership, and all related rights and interests of the remaining part of the Xudong Village urban village comprehensive renovation project (including the K plot development project, the H plot resettlement project, and the C plot industrial project), whether or not beyond the planning and design conditions, except for the 230,000 square meters of resettlement area to be delivered pursuant to the demolition and resettlement agreement, 15,000 square meters of commercial shops in the K1 plot, and 15,000 square meters of commercial shops in the C plot. Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company has the right to sell externally, and the corresponding sales funds shall be collected and enjoyed by Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company. If cooperation is required from this company for relevant procedures during the sales process, this company undertakes to handle them in a timely manner. Second, this company confirms that before the principal, interest, and other related rights and interests of the claims that your entity holds against Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company through entrusted loans are fully repaid, if Zhongsenhua Investment Company or Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company commits any breach of contract as stipulated in the Wuhan Hongshan District Xudong Village "Urban Village" Comprehensive Renovation Joint Development Contract, this company voluntarily waives the right to unilaterally terminate that contract as provided therein, but retains the right to demand compensation from Zhongsenhua Investment Company or Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company in accordance with that contract. Third, this company confirms that, except for fulfilling the obligations under the Wuhan Hongshan District Xudong Village "Urban Village" Comprehensive Renovation Joint Development Contract, Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company is not required to pay any transfer compensation to this company pursuant to the State-owned Construction Land Use Rights Transfer Compensation Contract signed between this company and Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company on December 30, 2010. Fourth, this company acknowledges and accepts the Supervision Agreement signed by your entity, Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company, and the supervisory bank, and undertakes to actively cooperate with the supervisory measures taken by your entity against Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company (including but not limited to the company's business activities, project construction, project sales, corporate finance, and accounts) in accordance with the Supervision Agreement, and not to interfere with the transfer or payment of funds within the "Sales Fund Supervision Account" established by Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company at your entity's request. Fifth, this company undertakes that all claims of this company against Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company shall rank junior to the claims (principal, interest, and other related rights and interests) that your party holds against Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company arising from the financing of RMB 630 million through entrusted loans. Sixth, this company undertakes that the equity interests held by this company in Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company shall not be transferred or pledged externally during the investment period of your entity. The above undertakings and commitments have been subject to lawful and effective decision-making and approval procedures by this company and shall take effect upon the seal of this company, producing full legal binding force on this company; these commitments shall remain valid until the full repayment of the principal and interest of the entrusted loan; without the written consent of your entity, this company shall not revoke, withdraw, amend, or terminate any of the commitments or matters committed.

This court holds that in this case, the Entrusted Loan Contract was signed by Changfu Fund, Industrial Bank Wuhan Branch, and Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company. Under this contract, Changfu Fund provided the funds, and Industrial Bank Wuhan Branch, acting on behalf of Changfu Fund and based on the borrower, purpose, amount, currency, term, and interest rate determined by Changfu Fund, disbursed the loan, assisted in supervising its use, and collected repayment. Industrial Bank Wuhan Branch collected a fee for acting as the agent for the entrusted loan and did not bear credit risk. In substance, this was a private lending relationship between Changfu Fund and Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company. The validity of the entrusted loan contract and the rights and obligations agreed upon between Changfu Fund and Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company should both be governed by the laws, regulations, and judicial interpretations relating to private lending. Article 1 of the Supreme People's Court's Notice on Seriously Studying and Implementing the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Private Lending Cases stipulates: "When a people's court determines the validity of a private lending contract, it shall, in accordance with the spirit of Article 3 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation (I) on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, apply these Provisions to private lending contracts concluded before the implementation of these Provisions if such contracts would be invalid under the judicial interpretations then in effect but would be valid under these Provisions." Article 11 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Private Lending Cases stipulates: "For private lending contracts concluded between legal persons, between other organizations, or between them for the needs of production and business operations, except where the circumstances specified in Article 52 of the Contract Law or Article 14 of these Provisions exist, if a party claims that the private lending contract is valid, the people's court shall support the claim." Article 14 stipulates: "If any of the following circumstances exists, the people's court shall find the private lending contract invalid: (1) obtaining credit funds from financial institutions and relending them to the borrower at a high interest rate, and the borrower knew or should have known of this; (2) obtaining funds from loans to other enterprises or from raising funds from the entity's own employees, and then relending them to the borrower for profit, and the borrower knew or should have known of this; (3) the lender knew or should have known that the borrower would use the loan for illegal or criminal activities but still provided the loan; (4) violating public order and good customs; (5) other circumstances that violate mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations regarding validity." In this case, the Entrusted Loan Contract signed by Changfu Fund and Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company through Industrial Bank Wuhan Branch does not violate the provisions of Article 52 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China or Article 14 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Private Lending Cases regarding contract invalidity. Therefore, regardless of whether it was before or after the implementation of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Private Lending Cases, the Entrusted Loan Contract involved in this case should be legally valid.

Based on the parties' appeal requests and defense opinions, the main issues in dispute in this case are as follows: First, whether Changfu Fund is a proper plaintiff in this case; Second, whether Changfu Fund bears liability for breach of contract in relation to the termination of the Entrusted Loan Contract; Third, whether the interest loss compensation to be paid by Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company from September 10, 2014, to the date of payment determined in this judgment should be calculated at an annual interest rate of 24%, and whether Changfu Fund's appeal request for liquidated damages of RMB 126 million can be upheld; Fourth, whether Changfu Fund can dispose of all of Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company's rights and interests in the C plot industrial project of Xudong Village urban village comprehensive renovation project of Xudong Group Company to satisfy the debts in this case; Fifth, whether the appraisal fee of RMB 110,000 should be borne by Changfu Fund or Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company. Based on the facts and evidence ascertained in this case, the analysis and evaluation of the above issues are as follows:

1. Regarding whether Changfu Fund is a proper plaintiff in this case. During the second instance trial, Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company submitted a supplementary appeal brief, relying on Article 1.4 of the Entrusted Loan Contract and the Supreme People's Court's Reply on How to Determine the Subject of Litigation in Disputes over Entrusted Loan Agreements, arguing that the court of first instance should not have accepted the lawsuit filed directly by Changfu Fund against Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company as the plaintiff. Changfu Fund argued in its defense that Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company's appeal request was submitted beyond the appeal period; Article 1.4 of the Entrusted Loan Contract was a permissive clause; the trustee bank also expressly stated in the first instance that it agreed with Changfu Fund's assertion of its rights; therefore, Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company's appeal argument that Changfu Fund was not a proper plaintiff in this case was unsustainable. This court holds that: First, Article 402 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "If an agent enters into a contract with a third party in the agent's own name within the scope of authorization of the principal, and the third party knows the agency relationship between the agent and the principal at the time of entering into the contract, the contract directly binds the principal and the third party, unless there is conclusive evidence that the contract only binds the agent and the third party." On September 27, 2013, Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company signed the Investment Cooperation Agreement with Changfu Fund, Industrial Bank Wuhan Branch, Zhongsenhua Investment Company, Zheng Juyun, and Chen Shaoxia, as well as the Entrusted Loan Contract with Changfu Fund and Industrial Bank Wuhan Branch. The content of these contracts indicates that, at the time of signing the Entrusted Loan Contract, Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company was aware of the agency relationship between Industrial Bank Wuhan Branch and Changfu Fund. Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company did not provide evidence to prove that the Entrusted Loan Contract only bound Industrial Bank Wuhan Branch and Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company. Therefore, the Entrusted Loan Contract directly binds Changfu Fund and Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company. The judgment of first instance, which found that Changfu Fund could assert its rights directly against Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company in its own name, has factual and legal basis. Second, Article 1.4 of the Entrusted Loan Contract, concerning the trustee's undertaking, provides: "If the borrower fails to repay the principal and interest on time, the trustee shall, at the written request of the principal, file a lawsuit in the name of the trustee against the borrower, guarantor, and related parties." This undertaking is a commitment made by the trustee, Industrial Bank Wuhan Branch, to the principal, Changfu Fund, and only binds Industrial Bank Wuhan Branch and Changfu Fund; it has nothing to do with Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company. As to the content of the undertaking, whether to file a lawsuit with Industrial Bank Wuhan Branch as the plaintiff against the borrower, guarantor, and related parties is a right granted to Changfu Fund under this undertaking, rather than an obligation limiting its actions. Changfu Fund may either file a lawsuit itself or request the trustee, Industrial Bank Wuhan Branch, to file a lawsuit. Furthermore, the Supreme People's Court's Reply on How to Determine the Subject of Litigation in Disputes over Entrusted Loan Agreements, in response to the relevant questions raised, states: "In the course of performing an entrusted loan agreement, if a dispute arises because the borrower fails to repay the loan on time, the lender (trustee) may file a lawsuit with the people's court on the grounds of a loan contract dispute; if the lender insists on not filing a lawsuit, the principal may file a lawsuit with the people's court against the trustee as the defendant and the borrower as the third party on the grounds of the entrusted loan agreement dispute." This reply provides that the principal may file a lawsuit as a plaintiff and clarifies the defendant status of the trustee, with the aim of protecting the principal's rights. Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company's appeal argument, based on the aforesaid provision and reply, that Changfu Fund is not a proper plaintiff in this case, is a misinterpretation of the contract provision and the reply, and is unsustainable. Third, Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company did not raise the issue of Changfu Fund not being a proper plaintiff in the first instance by way of counterclaim or defense. It only raised this appeal request during the second instance trial on March 21, 2016. The final appeal period for this case was December 25, 2015. Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company's submission of the appeal request during the second instance trial regarding Changfu Fund not being a proper plaintiff does not comply with Article 164 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides for a 15-day appeal period, nor with Article 328 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that in second instance proceedings, the plaintiff of the first instance may not add independent claims, nor may the defendant of the first instance file a counterclaim. In conclusion, Changfu Fund is a proper plaintiff in this case. Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company's appeal argument that Changfu Fund is not a proper plaintiff is not supported by this court.

2. Regarding whether Changfu Fund bears liability for breach of contract in relation to the termination of the Entrusted Loan Contract. Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company argues that Changfu Fund breached the contract by failing to disburse the second tranche of RMB 230 million to Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company, which caused funding difficulties for the project and significant losses to Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company, and that Changfu Fund should also bear responsibility for the termination of the Entrusted Loan Contract. Changfu Fund contends that it disbursed RMB 400 million in accordance with Article 2.1.3.1(1) of the Entrusted Loan Contract, but Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company failed to complete the mortgage registration as agreed, thus the conditions for disbursing the second tranche of RMB 230 million under Article 2.1.3.1(1) were not met. Changfu Fund did not breach the contract; on the contrary, it was Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company's breach that led to the termination of the Investment Cooperation Agreement and the Entrusted Loan Contract, and the responsibility lies entirely with Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company. This court holds that: First, Changfu Fund has already disbursed RMB 400 million in accordance with Article 2.1.3.1(1) of the Entrusted Loan Contract. Because Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company failed to complete mortgage registration for the K2, K3, and K4 plots and the projects under construction located in Xudong Village, Hongshan District, Wuhan City, Hubei Province, the conditions for disbursing the second tranche of RMB 230 million under Article 2.1.3.1(1) were not satisfied. Therefore, Changfu Fund and Industrial Bank Wuhan Branch did not breach the contract by not disbursing the second tranche of RMB 230 million. Second, Article 2.1.5.1 of the Entrusted Loan Contract provides: "Interest on the loan shall be calculated by natural quarter, with the interest payment date being the first working day after the 20th day of the last month of each quarter... The borrower must pay interest on each interest payment date." Article 2.1.7.2 provides: "If the borrower fails to repay the principal and interest within the term agreed in the contract, the principal shall charge penalty interest on the overdue amount from the due date at 50% above the agreed loan interest rate until the principal and interest are fully repaid." Article 4.1 of the Entrusted Loan Contract lists events of default by the borrower, including: failure to fulfill the undertakings in Article 1; expressly indicating or acting in a manner indicating unwillingness to repay matured or unmatured debts; failure to perform or fully perform obligations under other contracts signed between the borrower and the principal; the principal declaring the borrower in default; or other circumstances where the borrower fails to perform or fully perform the contract. Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company's failure to complete the mortgage registration for the K2, K3, and K4 plots and the projects under construction constitutes "failure to perform or fully perform obligations under other contracts signed between the borrower and the principal." After paying the interest for the first quarter of 2014, Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company failed to pay interest from March 22, 2014, and did not pay interest on a quarterly basis as agreed in the contract. This constitutes "expressly indicating or acting in a manner indicating unwillingness to repay matured or unmatured debts." At the time the court of first instance implemented the litigation preservation measures in this case, Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company was already involved in multiple lawsuits, and the collateral that was agreed to be provided to Changfu Fund under the contract had been sealed up by other creditors. Therefore, Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company committed a fundamental breach of contract. Changfu Fund's request to terminate the performance of the contract and accelerate the repayment of the loan complies with the provisions in the Investment Agreement and the Entrusted Loan Contract that "if the borrower or guarantor defaults, or if there may be a significant adverse change in the repayment ability of the borrower or guarantor, or if the collateral or pledged property may suffer significant damage or diminution in value, the loan disbursement may be stopped, and the disbursed loan may be accelerated for repayment." In conclusion, Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company shall bear the corresponding liability for breach of contract for the termination of the Entrusted Loan Contract involved in this case, while Changfu Fund bears no liability.

3. Concerning the issue of default interest and liquidated damages. Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company appealed arguing that the interest determined by the original judgment at an annual rate of 24% was excessively high, and that the interest loss from September 10, 2014 to the date of payment determined by this judgment should be calculated at an annual rate of 16%. Changfu Fund appealed arguing that Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company should also pay the liquidated damages of RMB 126 million as agreed. This Court holds: First, in the original trial, Changfu Fund claimed an annual rate of 16% for the period from March 22 to June 21, 2014, and an annual rate of 24% from June 22, 2014 onward, and demanded payment of RMB 126 million in liquidated damages from Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company. Based on the consideration of compensating for the actual losses suffered by Changfu Fund due to the rescission of the contract, the original judgment ordered Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company to compensate for the interest loss at an annual rate of 24% from the day after the original trial was accepted, i.e., September 10, 2014, to the date of payment determined by this judgment, and did not support Changfu Fund's claim for RMB 126 million in liquidated damages. Although the starting and ending dates and the interest rate standard for the calculation of interest loss in the original judgment were inconsistent with those claimed by Changfu Fund, Changfu Fund did not appeal against this, which should be regarded as a waiver of its relevant rights. Since Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company should bear liability for breach of contract for the rescission of the entrusted loan contract involved in the case, the overdue interest determined by the original judgment at an annual rate of 24% is also a method of bearing liability for breach of contract. The original judgment, taking into account factors such as the agreed liquidated damages and penalty interest in the contract, discretionarily determined that Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company should bear the interest loss at an annual rate of 24%, which is not obviously higher than the market financing cost and is not unfair to Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company. Therefore, this Court does not support Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company's appeal claim that the annual rate for interest loss should be calculated at 16%. Second, Article 27 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation (II) on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "Where a party requests the people's court to adjust the liquidated damages in accordance with the second paragraph of Article 114 of the Contract Law by way of a counterclaim or defense, the people's court shall support such request." Article 29 provides: "Where a party claims that the agreed liquidated damages are excessively high and requests appropriate reduction, the people's court shall, based on the actual losses, taking into account the performance of the contract, the degree of fault of the parties, expected benefits, and other comprehensive factors, measure and make a ruling in accordance with the principle of fairness and the principle of good faith." Article 30 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Private Lending Cases provides: "Where the lender and the borrower have agreed on both an overdue interest rate and liquidated damages or other fees, the lender may choose to claim overdue interest, liquidated damages, or other fees, or may claim them together, but the people's court shall not support the portion totaling more than 24% per annum." Article 3, paragraph 3, of the Supreme People's Court's Notice on Seriously Studying and Implementing the Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Private Lending Cases states: "After these Provisions come into effect, cases of first instance, second instance, and retrial that have not yet been concluded shall be tried in accordance with the judicial interpretations in effect before the implementation of these Provisions, and these Provisions shall not apply." Although, according to Article 3, paragraph 3, of the Supreme People's Court's Notice on Seriously Studying and Implementing the Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Private Lending Cases, the issues of interest and liquidated damages in the private lending relationship between Changfu Fund and Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company in this case should not be subject to the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Private Lending Cases, and the relevant laws, regulations, and judicial interpretations in effect previously did not restrict whether the lender could simultaneously claim overdue interest and liquidated damages or set a limit on the combination thereof. However, according to the spirit of Articles 27 and 29 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation (II) on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, where the overdue interest and liquidated damages in a private lending case concluded before the implementation of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Private Lending Cases are obviously excessive, and the party requests appropriate reduction on the ground that the agreed liquidated damages are excessively high, the court may also refer to the judicial protection upper limit of 24% per annum established by the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Private Lending Cases for adjustment. In addition to the overdue interest at an annual rate of 24% determined by the original judgment, Changfu Fund claims liquidated damages of RMB 126 million in accordance with the contract. This claim essentially seeks the parallel application of overdue penalty interest and fixed liquidated damages. In this case, the losses suffered by Changfu Fund due to Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company's breach are primarily interest losses. Since Changfu Fund has not provided evidence proving that its actual losses exceed the overdue interest determined by the original judgment, this Court does not support its appeal claim that Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company should pay an additional RMB 126 million in liquidated damages on top of the overdue interest determined by the original judgment.

4. Concerning the issue of whether Changfu Fund may dispose of all of Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company's rights and interests in the C plot industrial project of Xudong Group Company's Xudong Village urban village comprehensive renovation project to satisfy the debts in this case. Changfu Fund appealed requesting a judgment that it has the right to dispose of all of Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company's rights and interests in the C plot industrial project involved in the case to satisfy the debts in this case. Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company and Xudong Group Company argued in their defenses that whether Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company has rights and interests in the C plot industrial project involved in the case and whether Changfu Fund has the right to dispose of them are not within the scope of trial of this case. This Court holds: In the Letter of Commitment No. 2013 (Century) 12, Xudong Group Company confirmed that the land use rights, construction in progress, ownership of buildings, and all related rights and interests in the C plot industrial project, except for 15,000 square meters of shops, belong to Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company. This expression of intent is clear and definite. The Letter of Commitment does not state that Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company enjoys these rights and interests subject to additional conditions. There is no issue as argued by Xudong Group Company in its defense that Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company could only obtain property rights after satisfying three conditions for joint development, and that Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company's rights in the plot were merely a possibility. Furthermore, in the Letter of Commitment, Xudong Group Company also undertook that all its claims against Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company would be subordinated to the claims of Changfu Fund. From the perspective of the obligations set forth in the Letter of Commitment, it constitutes a guarantee-type commitment made by Xudong Group Company to Changfu Fund regarding the claims under the entrusted loan contract. Although it does not have the effect of an exclusive property right under property law and cannot be asserted against third parties, this commitment does not violate the prohibitive provisions of laws and regulations, should be legally valid, and is binding between the parties. Therefore, the arguments of Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company and Xudong Group Company that whether Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company has rights and interests in the C plot industrial project involved in the case and whether Changfu Fund has the right to dispose of them are not within the scope of trial of this case cannot be sustained. Changfu Fund's claim in this case for the right to dispose of all of Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company's rights and interests in the C plot industrial project involved in the case to satisfy the debts in this case should be supported. As for the rights and obligations relationship between Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company and Xudong Group Company in the C plot industrial project involved in the case, it shall be separately determined in accordance with the relevant contracts between the company and Xudong Group Company, and has no impact on Changfu Fund's rights in the C plot industrial project involved in the case. How Changfu Fund disposes of all of Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company's rights and interests in the C plot industrial project involved in the case is not within the scope of resolution in this case. Any disputes with others arising from such disposal shall be resolved in separate proceedings or in the enforcement process.

5. Concerning the issue of the RMB 110,000 appraisal fee. Changfu Fund appealed arguing that the Letter of Commitment of Zhongsen Company was submitted by Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company to Changfu Fund, and the appraisal fee incurred due to the verification of the falsity of the seal and signature on the Letter of Commitment should be borne by Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company. Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company argued in its defense that it is impossible to determine whether the Letter of Commitment of Zhongsen Company submitted by Changfu Fund in this litigation is consistent with the one delivered by Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company to Changfu Fund, and the appraisal fee should be borne by Changfu Fund, the party submitting the evidence. This Court holds: Although the disputed RMB 110,000 appraisal fee was incurred for the appraisal of the Letter of Commitment of Zhongsen Company, the appraisal conclusion did not confirm that the Letter of Commitment was issued by Zhongsen Company. Therefore, Zhongsen Company should not bear the appraisal fee. Since Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company admitted the fact that it submitted the Letter of Commitment of Zhongsen Company to Changfu Fund, Changfu Fund had no reason not to submit this Letter of Commitment of Zhongsen Company in the litigation to support its claims. Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company should bear the corresponding burden of proof for its defense claim that the Letter of Commitment subject to appraisal is inconsistent with the Letter of Commitment it submitted to Changfu Fund; otherwise, it should bear adverse consequences. Since Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company has no supporting evidence for its defense claim, this Court supports Changfu Fund's appeal claim that the RMB 110,000 appraisal fee should be borne by Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company.

In addition, in its defense brief, Beilong Company argued that it had never issued to Changfu Fund or any third party a commitment subordinating its priority right to payment for construction project costs. The original judgment found that Changfu Fund had priority right to the auction proceeds of the project contracted and constructed by Beilong Company, which conflicts with the civil judgment of the Hubei High People's Court (2013) E Min Yi Chu Zi No. 00011. Beilong Company claimed that Changfu Fund should compensate it for transportation expenses, travel expenses, attorney fees, etc., totaling RMB 100,000, and requested that Changfu Fund's claim for priority right to the auction proceeds of Xudong Apartment constructed by Beilong Company be dismissed. This Court holds: First, the original judgment found that the seal of Beilong Company and the signature of its legal representative, Chen Shutian, affixed to Beilong Company's Letter of Commitment were determined to be forged by the Zhongxing Notary Office of Wuhan City, Hubei Province, and therefore held that the Letter of Commitment was not binding on Beilong Company. Accordingly, in its judgment, the original judgment did not support Changfu Fund's claim for confirmation of the validity of Beilong Company's Letter of Commitment No. 2013 (Century) 7-1 and the subordination of Beilong Company's right to payment for construction project costs in the Xudong Village urban village comprehensive renovation project to Changfu Fund's claims. Since Changfu Fund and Beilong Company did not appeal against this part, this Court does not comment on the issue of whether Beilong Company issued a commitment subordinating its priority right to payment for construction project costs to Changfu Fund or any third party. Second, the original judgment's decision that Changfu Fund has the priority right to receive compensation from the proceeds of the discount, auction, or sale of 10,325.82 square meters of the Xudong Apartment building at Xudong Village, Hongshan District, Wuhan City, Hubei Province, was based on the mortgage contract between Industrial Bank Wuhan Branch and Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company and the Wuhan City Forward Housing Mortgage Certificate (Wu Fang Qi Hong Zi No. 2013015485), not on Beilong Company's Letter of Commitment. Therefore, there is no contradiction as argued by Beilong Company that the original judgment confirmed that the Letter of Commitment of Beilong Company submitted by Changfu Fund was forged but also recognized that Changfu Fund had priority right to the auction proceeds of the project contracted and constructed by Beilong Company. Third, as to whether the original judgment's decision that Changfu Fund has the priority right to receive compensation from the proceeds of the discount, auction, or sale of 10,325.82 square meters of the Xudong Apartment building at Xudong Village, Hongshan District, Wuhan City, Hubei Province conflicts with Beilong Company's priority right to payment for construction project costs as determined in the civil judgment of the Hubei High People's Court (2013) E Min Yi Chu Zi No. 00011, and whether Changfu Fund should compensate Beilong Company for transportation expenses, travel expenses, attorney fees, etc., totaling RMB 100,000, since Beilong Company did not raise these two claims by way of appeal and they are not within the scope of trial of this case, they shall be resolved separately in the enforcement process or other proceedings.

In conclusion, Changfu Fund's appeal is partially sustained, and this Court supports it. Zhongsenhua Real Estate Company's appeal claims cannot be sustained, and this Court dismisses them. Pursuant to Article 170, paragraph 1, item (2) and Article 175 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. Affirm items 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 of the civil judgment (2014) E Min Er Chu Zi No. 00035 of the Hubei High People's Court;

2. Reverse item 7 of the civil judgment (2014) E Min Er Chu Zi No. 00035 of the Hubei High People's Court;

3. The Letter of Commitment No. 2013 (Century) 12 issued by Hubei Xudong (Group) Co., Ltd. is legally valid. Beijing Changfu Investment Fund (Limited Partnership) has the right to dispose of all rights and interests of Wuhan Zhongsenhua Century Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. in the C plot industrial project of the Xudong Village urban village comprehensive renovation project of Hubei Xudong (Group) Co., Ltd. to satisfy the debts in this case;

4. Dismiss the other claims of Beijing Changfu Investment Fund (Limited Partnership).

Court acceptance fees for the first instance shall be executed in accordance with the first instance judgment. The appraisal fee of RMB 110,000 shall be borne by Wuhan Zhongsenhua Century Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. The second instance appeal case acceptance fee of RMB 546,540 for Beijing Changfu Investment Fund (Limited Partnership) and the second instance appeal case acceptance fee of RMB 255,133.33 for Wuhan Zhongsenhua Century Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. shall be borne respectively by Beijing Changfu Investment Fund (Limited Partnership) and Wuhan Zhongsenhua Century Real Estate Development Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
